## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On uses changes in the distance between its two satellites to help investigate water movement on Earth. The satellites follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart.

As they pass a larger mass concentration, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite. The changing separation is used to infer shifts in mass.

Those inferred shifts can reveal changes in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
